title: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks
summary: IIT Gandhinagar proposes learned traffic forecasts and GNN/DRL policies to support adaptive routing, alongside conventional network optimization.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The framework combines learned traffic prediction and a proposed graph-neural-network/deep-reinforcement-learning policy with classical routing optimization. The intended AI contribution is better anticipation of demand and more adaptive routing decisions. Simulation and evaluation are planned. The source does not report an attributable operator energy saving, and conventional optimization is not counted separately as an AI benefit.
purpose: Use learned demand forecasts and routing policies to allocate network resources efficiently.
system: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks

ratings.reason: More efficient routing through learned forecasts and policies is intended; no attributable operator energy or throughput improvement is reported.
Lower emissions resulting from AI-assisted network decisions remain intended.

ai_role.statement: Traffic models predict demand; GNN/DRL policies are proposed for adaptive decisions in larger networks.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 11: AI-Assisted Smart and Efficient Radio Access Networks

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.

headline: Learned traffic prediction aims to improve network routing
